skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

14. 
15. ### Verification (commands run + evidence)
16. 
17. **`make verify-kernel`** → Exit code 0. All modules verify:
18. `mm::phys`, `mm::phys::frame`, `mm::phys::kframe`, `mm::phys::manager`, `mm::phys::upool`.
19. Cheating check: `assume=0 external_body=22 admit=2 trusted=0`. Cross-module regression PASS.
20. 
21. **Cheating detail** (`verus-logs/cheating-detail.txt`) — manager-owned items:
22. - `manager.rs` `external_body` ×6: `init`, `alloc_many_user_frames`, `alloc_user_frame`,
23.   `check_user_watermark`, `alloc_kernel_frame`, `alloc_many_kernel_frames`.
24.   All six are explicitly enumerated in `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md` (stateless-facade
25.   rationale, mirrors the `frame.rs` free-function shims). → PASS for this phase.
26. - `manager.proof.rs` `admit` ×2: `lemma_watermark_monotone`, `lemma_contiguous_run_distinct`.
27.   Proof file header states bodies are `admit()` in the spec-design phase, discharged in the
28.   proving phase. → acceptable for the specification phase.
29. 
30. **`fn_coverage` (in-scope):** the 6 verification-order targets each carry `#[verus_spec]`
31. with `requires`/`ensures`. `get_mut` is on the tcb-allowed skip list (caller_analysis.md
32. §"Script-output corrections"), not a target. → PASS.
33. 
34. **`grep assume_specification src/kernel/src/mm/phys/`** → none. → PASS.
35. 
36. **View consistency:** specs are stated over `phys_view()` / `FrameAllocView` and re-establish
37. `phys_view().inv()` + `phys_view().initialized`. This deviates from the `self@`-View in
38. `view_design.md`, but the deviation is documented (manager.spec.rs header + view_design.md
39. implementation note: a field-less facade's `view(&self)` is constant, so it cannot witness
40. global mutation; there is no `old(phys_view())`). The same monotone style is used by the
41. already-accepted `frame::book` / `frame::alloc_range` shims (verified). → PASS.
42. 
43. **No-tautological / Error-paths (NOTE, not actionable):** `alloc_user_frame`,
44. `alloc_kernel_frame`, and `check_user_watermark` use `Err(_) => true`. This is literally the
45. checklist's bad example. However: (a) the sibling shims `frame::book` and `frame::alloc_range`
46. (frame.rs:776, 821) use the identical `Err(_) => true`; (b) strengthening the Err arm of a
47. `phys_view()`-style shim requires `old(phys_view())`, which Verus cannot express for a nullary
48. `spec fn`. The bulk fns already carry a meaningful Err arm (`final(frames)@.len() == 0`).
49. I am therefore NOT requesting a change here — it is consistent with established module
50. precedent and unstrengthenable. (If the fixer disagrees, show tool output proving a stronger
51. Err arm type-checks.)
52. 
53. ---
54. 
55. ### FAIL — Caller coverage: the watermark policy split is missing from the user-alloc specs
56. 
57. **Evidence (byte-identical ensures):**
58. `alloc_user_frame` (manager.rs:253-262) and `alloc_kernel_frame` (manager.rs:338-347) have
59. **character-for-character identical** `ensures`:
60. ```
61. ensures
62.     phys_view().inv(),
63.     phys_view().initialized,
64.     match result {
65.         Ok(frame) => {
66.             &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
67.             &&& frame@ % spec_page_size() == 0
68.         },
69.         Err(_) => true,
70.     },
71. ```
72. The same holds for `alloc_many_user_frames` vs `alloc_many_kernel_frames`: they differ ONLY by
73. the contiguity conjunct, not by any watermark fact.
74. 
75. **Why this is a defect (not a style nit):**
76. - `caller_analysis.md` lists the watermark as a KEY invariant and states explicitly, for
77.   `alloc_user_frame`: *"Would break callers: skipping the watermark check (the doc/comment at
78.   the call site explicitly relies on this single-frame helper keeping the watermark gate)."*
79. - `view_design.md` mapping table requires `alloc_user_frame` success to depend on
80.   `spec_watermark_ok(self@, 1)` and explicitly specifies the kernel variants **without** it.
81. - The entire reason `check_user_watermark` exists is the user/kernel policy split. Yet a caller
82.   reading `alloc_user_frame`'s contract cannot conclude the allocation respected
83.   `KERNEL_WATERMARK`. The user contract is presently indistinguishable from the
84.   watermark-bypassing kernel contract. The load-bearing guarantee is invisible.
85. - This is statable **without** `old(phys_view())`: `check_user_watermark(count)` guarantees
86.   `free_count >= KERNEL_WATERMARK + count` *before* servicing; after handing out `count` frames,
87.   `free' = free - count >= KERNEL_WATERMARK`, i.e. `spec_watermark_ok(phys_view().frames, 0)`.
88. 
89. ### Fix Request
90. 
91. Strengthen the **user** allocation contracts (and only those) so the watermark policy is
92. caller-observable. Leave the **kernel** contracts unchanged (they bypass the watermark).
93. 
94. 1. In `manager.rs::alloc_user_frame` `ensures`, add to the `Ok` arm (and add the finiteness
95.    fact the watermark predicate needs, since `PhysMemView::inv` does NOT imply finiteness —
96.    `mod.spec.rs:105` `inv := initialized ==> frames.wf()`, and `FrameAllocView::wf` has no
97.    `finite()` conjunct):
98.    ```
99.    Ok(frame) => {
100.        &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
101.        &&& frame@ % spec_page_size() == 0
102.        &&& phys_view().frames.free_frames.finite()
103.        &&& spec_watermark_ok(phys_view().frames, 0)
104.    },
105.    ```
106. 
107. 2. In `manager.rs::alloc_many_user_frames` `ensures`, add the same two conjuncts
108.    (`free_frames.finite()` and `spec_watermark_ok(phys_view().frames, 0)`) to its `Ok(())` arm.
109. 
110. 3. Do **NOT** add these to `alloc_kernel_frame` or `alloc_many_kernel_frames` — the kernel
111.    variants must remain watermark-free so their contracts stay distinct (and correct: kernel
112.    allocation may legitimately drive free frames below the watermark).
113. 
114. **Verify the fix with:**
115. - `make verify-kernel` → must remain Exit 0 (all modules, no new errors).
116. - `diff` the two single-frame `ensures` blocks: they must NO LONGER be identical
117.   (`sed -n '253,262p'` vs `sed -n '338,347p' src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs`).
118. - Confirm `spec_watermark_ok` and `phys_view` are in scope in `manager.rs` (they are used
119.   already by `check_user_watermark`, so no new imports needed).
120. 
121. Justification is not a fix: if you believe the watermark cannot be stated in the post-state,
122. show the Verus error from attempting conjunct (3) above — otherwise change the code.
